diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Today marks the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. On this day, routes leading to Aichi Cemetery in Saqez were blocked, and merchants in 13 cities including Saqez and Sanandaj went on strike. Security forces' presence in Saqez has also increased.

After a strike in Kurdish cities, a security atmosphere has been established. Mahan Airlines flights to Turkey and Oman have been canceled. This was mentioned in the audio version of Titraval with Niousha Saremi.

The US Treasury Department held a meeting with international financial institutions to advance the economic exclusion operation. The goal is to isolate Tehran and limit its ability to finance the war in the Middle East. Necessary information to cut off revenue streams related to the Iranian government was provided during the meeting.

Reuters reported that American officials met with Houthi representatives in Oman. CENTCOM also confirmed a secret meeting between military commanders from the US, Israel, and eight Arab countries to discuss the war in Iran. This information was sourced from five informed officials.

Ange Postecoglou, Al Nassr's coach, defended Cristiano Ronaldo after their 4-0 loss to Al Ain. He said the responsibility is his but Ronaldo remains a role model and the players gave their best. Al Nassr suffered Ronaldo's heaviest defeat in Saudi Arabia in the AFC Champions League.

The Alaj website, created to identify opponents of the Islamic Republic abroad, has gone offline. The reason is unclear and may be due to domain blocking or technical issues. The technical team stated that due to high traffic and cyberattacks, the site was temporarily taken offline.

The third session of the trial of Mehran Mohagheghi, accused of driving a car into a crowd at an Iranian protest in Richmond Hill, ended without a verdict. The incident occurred on May 10 in Richmond Hill, Toronto, and Mohagheghi was arrested after causing damage and threatening attendees. The case is still ongoing.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad said the Women, Life, Freedom movement was an exceptional revolution that became a turning point in the history of the Islamic Republic. He added that the consequences of this movement, from increased repression to subsequent developments, stem from the government's response to the 1401 protests. He also noted that the repression of protests and the return of security figures indicate a change in the Islamic Republic's approach after this movement.

At least 300 faculty members of Farhangian University have not received their salaries for over a year and are in an uncertain employment status. Some of these professors are protesting forced retirement. This state of uncertainty continues.

American diplomats met with Houthi representatives in the US embassy in Muscat to discuss tensions in the Red Sea. The talks focused on continuing the ceasefire and ensuring the Bab al-Mandeb Strait remains open. Houthi representatives stated their attacks target only Saudi ships.
This news refers to Russia's role in the Islamic Republic's attack on the US base. No further details about this role are provided. The topic discusses Russia's influence in this attack.

Amin Shirafkan and Alireza Hajtemand were arrested by security forces in Gorgan. The arrest took place on the morning of Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, at Shirafkan's workplace. Both were transferred to the Gorgan police detention center.

A citizen sent a video on Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, showing ready-to-distribute food containers. He stated that he is distributing these foods among the needy in memory of the martyrs of the Mahsa uprising.

Workers' wages are equivalent to the cost of living for only eight days. This indicates a significant gap between income and living expenses. The livelihood of workers is severely affected by this issue.

Reza Pahlavi, on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death, stated that the Iranian nation is in a new phase of struggle to reclaim Iran. He mentioned the deaths of other protesters and described recent uprisings as part of the revolutionary path. Pahlavi emphasized that the current opposition solidarity is the result of a long and costly journey and vowed to continue the path of the deceased.

Esteghlal club will form a women's volleyball team with Niloufar Hojati as head coach. Hojati was a coach for the Iranian women's national volleyball team in the 2026 Asian Championship. Additionally, Esteghlal has reached an agreement with Fatemeh Khalili, a player of the Iranian women's national volleyball team.

Air traffic control tower staff across the country went on strike from the evening of Tuesday, September 14 to the night of Wednesday, September 15. This strike caused widespread disruption and several hours of delay in flights. Pilots in some cases waited between half an hour to two hours to receive clearance from the control tower.

The third edition of the international film festival "Woman, Life, Freedom" began on the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death. Unlike previous years, this edition is not limited to one city and is held in various locations worldwide. The festival is also held online to reach a wider audience.

Wang Yi, China's foreign minister, during a meeting with Abbas Araghchi, called for restraint from Tehran and Washington and a swift return to the Islamabad understanding. He also emphasized the need for the rapid reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring the security of international waterways. The Chinese foreign minister stated that China will continue efforts to establish peace and stability in the Middle East.

Siamak Aram stated that the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement has helped form more cohesive networks among the Iranian diaspora. This movement has facilitated coordinated gatherings and activities in various cities worldwide. Additionally, diaspora activities have changed Western officials' rhetoric, but this change has not yet translated into practical policies.

Antonio Guterres condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and disruptions in shipping routes. He emphasized the need to maintain freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab according to international law. Guterres warned that the escalation of the crisis could have broader security and humanitarian consequences.

The foreign ministers of Israel and Morocco agreed in a trilateral meeting with the US ambassador to the UN to enhance bilateral relations. The agreement includes upgrading diplomatic representations, increasing flights, and holding high-level meetings. They also agreed to finalize agreements on investment protection and double taxation prevention by the end of 2026.

A citizen stated in a video to Iran International that after an accident, they need to buy a car radiator for seven million tomans. This indicates the rising inflation in Iran. The price of car parts has increased significantly.

Turkish and Pakistani officials stated that Saudi Arabia has not requested help from these two countries following intensified Houthi attacks. The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure are the first test of the new defense pact among these countries. The Houthis have denied targeting Mecca.

The CENTCOM spokesperson stated that the US military has achieved its objectives against the Islamic Republic and weakened Iran's missile and drone capabilities. He said the Iranian navy is practically destroyed and Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, the main shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared and are open.

AC Milan lost 2-0 to Benfica in their first match of the new Europa League season. Benfica won at San Siro against Milan for the first time in their history. Goals by Dodi Lukebakio and Kaminski led to this defeat.

Manchester United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the third round of the English League Cup and was eliminated. This is the first time in 50 years that Manchester United has lost at home after leading by two goals. Some fans stayed in the stadium after the match and protested.

A citizen reported that the Tehran to Sulaymaniyah flight was delayed at Imam Khomeini Airport due to lack of flight clearance. The pilot stated that because there is no radar in the country, they have to estimate the route, causing delays in issuing the clearance.

Mahan Airlines has suspended its international flights to Turkey and Oman until further notice. This decision was made after the United States imposed new sanctions on Mahan Air's support network. The news was reported in an interview with Amir Giti on Iran International.

Four years after the killing of Mahsa Jina Amini, Iranian women have reclaimed part of their right to choose in the streets, but this right is not yet guaranteed by law. Women discuss their experience of going out without a headscarf and the costs they have paid. This topic was covered in the September 16 special program on Iran International.

The American company Poweras has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Pakistan Army and received an initial order related to unmanned aerial systems. This news was released simultaneously with a delegation from Poweras meeting the Pakistan Army commander. Details of the order or the type of unmanned systems were not disclosed.

Barcelona defeated Racing Santander 7-2 in the sixth week of La Liga. The team recorded its seventh consecutive win in seven official games this season and set a new record with 28 goals in the first six weeks. Rafinha scored a hat-trick and leads the La Liga top scorers.

During the first week of Iran's League One football match between Basat Kermanshah and Naft o Gaz Gachsaran, referees' belongings including mobile phones, gold, and cash were stolen from the locker room. The stolen items were valued at over 500 million tomans. This incident caused a 40-minute delay in the game, and after the match, the referees left the stadium without compensation.

The US embassy in Yemen reiterated its support for the internationally recognized government of Yemen. Jonathan Hop confirmed Washington's support in talks with Yemen's foreign minister. The US stands with the Yemeni government against attacks by the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic.

Shahad Alavi from Iran International said the recent Amnesty International report attributes responsibility for repression to local and provincial officials as well. The report shows that being part of the command chain can create legal responsibility. It is no longer possible to avoid accountability by arguing that one was not directly involved in the repression.

The US House of Representatives approved a bill extending the Iran Sanctions Act (ISA) until the end of 2031. Currently, the law is valid until the end of 2026, and its extension maintains the legal framework for sanctions on parts of Iran's economy. This bill will take effect after the US president signs it.

Donald Trump will meet with Gulf leaders next Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The main focus of the meeting is to discuss the US strategy after the war with the Islamic Republic. Foreign ministers of the six GCC countries will attend the session.

Choo Hyun, South Korea's foreign minister, stated that Seoul has not yet decided on sending military forces to the Strait of Hormuz. These remarks were made on Thursday, September 17. He made these comments before traveling to Washington.

ABC News, citing a US Department of Homeland Security intelligence bulletin, reported that the Islamic Republic likely intends to target the industrial control systems used by American energy companies to monitor storage tanks in cyber attacks. According to the bulletin, such attacks could lead to physical damage or fuel and chemical leaks. The US Department of Homeland Security also stated that Iranian cyber actors used DeepSeek AI in early August to research storage tank capacities in the United States.

Joe Wilson, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, welcomed the passage of the 'Lindsey Graham 2026 Russia and Iran Sanctions Act'. The House passed the bill on Wednesday with 262 votes in favor and 159 against, sending it to President Donald Trump for signature. The legislation extends the authorization of Iran sanctions until 2031.

Yasmin Ansari commemorated Mahsa Jina Amini on the fourth anniversary of her death. She mentioned the killing of thousands of protesters, political prisoners, and executions. Ansari emphasized continuing the fight for freedom and human rights in Iran.

Anwar Ibrahim, the Prime Minister of Malaysia, condemned the interception of a drone near Mecca, calling it a threat to the security of the holy city. He praised Saudi Arabia for its swift action to protect Mecca and called for restraint and dialogue. The Saudi-led coalition destroyed the drone and attributed the attack to the Houthis, who denied involvement.

Times of Israel reported that the Lod District Court sentenced Alexander Granovsky, a resident of Petah Tikva, to 13 and a half years in prison for espionage, property destruction, and arson on behalf of the Islamic Republic. According to the report, in exchange for money from an Iranian agent, he set nine cars on fire, wrote anti-government slogans, and surveilled the neighborhood where former Israeli Defense Minister Benny Gantz resides. The Central District Attorney's Office declared this the heaviest punishment yet for acting on behalf of Iran.

The economic crisis caused by the war in Iran has forced thousands of Afghan migrants to return to their country. Sharp price increases and the devaluation of the rial have wiped out much of their savings. More than two million Afghans have left Iran in the past two years.

Reuters reported that the number of cargo ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday dropped to 3 vessels. This is significantly lower than the daily average of about 17 vessels over the past 10 days. The data is based on shipping information.

The New York Times reported that US intelligence officers expressed concern about possible Chinese espionage in the potential $24 billion sale of dozens of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia has decades of military cooperation with the US, but it buys ballistic missiles from China and the Chinese military helps Riyadh build missiles. A Pentagon report stressed that only Saudi and American officers and contractors should have access to sites where F-35 technology is kept.

The US House of Representatives approved a five-year extension of Iran sanctions law, including restrictions on investment in the energy sector and provision of goods and services to oil and petrochemical industries. This law is considered the oldest pillar of Iran's energy sanctions. According to Miad Maleki, this law deters major oil companies like Shell and Total from entering Iran's refining sector.

Mojtaba Yousefi stated that rising oil prices can act as a deterrent against the US, but some officials' stances have led to a decrease in oil prices. He described oil prices as a decisive factor in the resistance axis. Regarding the Islamabad agreement, he said staying in the deal after the US withdrawal is neither dignified diplomacy nor wise.

Amir Giti stated that the Iranian government will retreat from Trump's demands only if its financial resources and economic interests are at risk. He added that economic pressure has increased but the government has not yet yielded. These remarks were made regarding the Islamic Republic's willingness to negotiate and the impact of economic pressures.

Shayan Samiei referred to a CNN report about the possible transfer of Russian satellite information to Iran before the attack on Prince Sultan base. If this cooperation is confirmed, Russia's role will go beyond political support and military cooperation. Moscow would effectively enter Iran's intelligence and targeting chain.

The documentary "Naza," shown at the Venice Film Festival, presents the accounts of 24 Israeli officers and soldiers about military operations in Gaza. It claims an attack was approved with the anticipation of killing 500 civilians, which the Israeli army has denied. The film has sparked debate about the army's conduct and freedom of expression in Israel.
Abdolbaset Bapiri, a citizen from Oshnavieh, was arrested by security forces in Piranshahr on Tuesday, September 14. He was transferred to an unknown location. No further details have been released.

Peyman Falsafi, Tehran representative, stated that the Islamic Republic will neutralize any US military threat with faith and hidden defensive capabilities. He added that economic sanctions have strengthened the will of the Iranian nation. The enemy fears entering a military war due to Iran's defensive capabilities.

A video shows the situation of Fly Kish passengers in Istanbul after the sanctions on Iranian airlines. Passengers had to board the plane from an underground corridor early Thursday morning. This occurred outside the usual area and conditions of Istanbul Airport.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated at the Iranian University Professors' Assembly that with inflation over 60 to 70 percent, a 20 percent salary increase is insufficient. He highlighted economic problems and inflation, noting there is no simple solution. He also expressed hope that the enemy will adhere to the commitments made in the memorandum of understanding.
A video showing the deployment of officers on a street in Shiraz has been released. The video depicts a security atmosphere in the city. The video is silent.

Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in the Campeones Cup final, where his team defeated Cruz Azul 2-0. Messi also assisted Casemiro's goal. This championship marks Messi's 49th professional career title.

Rouhollah Rahimpour commented on Trump's statements about Iran's willingness to reach an agreement and the possibility of ending the war before the midterm elections. He said that changing the timing of the war's end does not necessarily mean a change in goals or reaching an agreement. He also emphasized that it cannot be said with certainty that the government has decided to end the war through an agreement.

Amir Ghalenoei announced the first list of Premier League players for the national football team after the World Cup. In this list, Mohammad Hossein Kanaani Zadegan and Roozbeh Cheshmi, the two captains of the rival teams, are absent. Three goalkeepers and several defenders and midfielders have been invited to the national team.

Narges Mohammadi spoke to CNN about torture, medical deprivation, and efforts to smuggle her writings out of Evin prison. Her memoir titled "A Woman Never Gives Up the Fight" will be published this month in several European countries. Mohammadi emphasized that exposing torture methods is essential to document the truth.

The Iran Human Rights Organization released a list of over 4,200 casualties from the January 2026 protests. Among the identified dead are at least 420 women and 281 children under 18. Additionally, 91% of the deaths occurred on January 8 and 9 and were recorded in 30 provinces.

Naser Bahmiyari, a 67-year-old resident of Karaj, was arrested on Tuesday, September 14, by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization. He was transferred to an unknown location. The arrest took place at his private residence.

Mohammadreza Bahonar stated that a full-scale military war will not occur, though limited attacks may continue. He based this analysis on the balance of gains and losses in previous clashes. According to him, bombing cities like Tehran and Isfahan will not happen.

On the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death and the start of the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' movement, thousands of Iranian women shared their feelings after abandoning the mandatory hijab. These conversations highlight the impact of this event on their lives. The interview was conducted with Seba Heidarkhani, a member of Iran International's editorial team.

Houthi forces affiliated with the Islamic Republic in Yemen announced that they have shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. A video was released showing the wreckage of the fighter jet. The exact model of the aircraft is not identifiable due to extensive damage.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, stated that no government has the right to force others to surrender. He emphasized that they will not bow to oppression and tyranny. This position has been clearly declared.
A video shows that on the early morning of 25 Shahrivar, a long queue for gasoline formed in front of the Ghadir fuel station in Birjand.
Four women's hair salons in Kashan were closed due to non-compliance with Islamic codes and issues related to online activities.

Azadi Stadium in Tehran is still under renovation, with areas like tunnels and stands remaining unusable. It was previously planned to be ready for the 1406–1405 season, but replacing the turf has extended the preparation process. The exact time for the stadium's reopening is still unknown.

The UN fact-finding mission reported that the US committed war crimes in two airstrikes on Iran. These attacks killed at least 178 civilians, including children. One attack targeted a primary school in Minab and the other a residential area in Lamerd.

The prices of essential and non-food goods are increasing daily. The cost of medicine and hygiene products has also risen. People complain about the high prices and inability to afford essential items.

Mohammadreza Entezami, 29 years old, was shot dead on the evening of January 8 in Haft Hoz, Tehran. His last handwritten note has been published. In this short text, he wrote that everything always gets better.

The UN fact-finding mission reported that during the suppression of protests in 2025 and 2026 in Iran, security forces killed protesters in 31 provinces. The highest number of deaths were reported in Tehran, Karaj, Mashhad, Isfahan, and Rasht. At least 221 children, including a two-year-old, were killed in these crackdowns.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation rejected Persepolis's complaint about Yaser Asani's presence in Esteghlal's lineup. The committee, based on the Transfer Committee's opinion, recognized Asani as an active and eligible player. Asani's contract with Esteghlal was deemed valid, and his participation in matches was not considered unauthorized.

On Sunday, 15 Shahrivar, the home of Saeed Azimi, a Bahá'í citizen in Isfahan, was searched by intelligence officers. The officers confiscated his electronic and personal belongings during the search. This report was published by HRANA news agency.

Matin Ghorbani was killed by the bullets of the Islamic Republic's suppression forces during national protests in Karaj on January 8. His name remains in the memory of this land. His memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

A video shows security forces present around the City Center commercial complex in Bandar Abbas on the evening of September 16. The video was sent to Iran International. The location is the city center of Bandar Abbas.

Iran's Foreign Ministry summoned the Swedish ambassador in Tehran and demanded that a Swedish diplomat leave Iran within 48 hours in response to Sweden expelling an Iranian diplomat. The Swedish government also summoned the Iranian ambassador and asked an Iranian diplomat to leave Sweden. Sweden's Foreign Ministry stated that the diplomat's activities were not in accordance with the Vienna Convention on diplomatic relations.

Hossein Aghaei said that the Islamic Republic and the US are currently trying to remain below the threshold of full-scale war. He added that Tehran is using time to open new fronts and strengthen its military capabilities. Continued economic and sanction pressures could turn this time to the disadvantage of the Islamic Republic.

On the early morning of Tuesday, 23 Shahrivar, the execution of a female prisoner named Rezvan Asgharzadeh was carried out in Dastgerd Prison, Isfahan. She was sentenced for drug-related crimes. This sentence had been confirmed by the Supreme Court.

Morteza Kazemian reacted to Mohammad Reza Bahonar's definition of all-out war. He said Bahonar considers a serious war to be the bombing of Tehran or Isfahan. This view indicates discrimination among Iranian citizens.

Asghar Rahimi, head of Iran's sports delegation, announced that Iran aims to win at least 20 gold medals at the Nagoya Asian Games. The Iranian delegation includes 308 male and female athletes. The goal is to achieve better results compared to the previous games where 13 gold medals were won.

New images show that the renovation of Azadi Stadium has not been completed after about three years. The final cost of the project is estimated at around five thousand billion tomans. The timeline for the stadium's return to hosting football matches has been changed multiple times.

Flights of Saman Airlines from Iran to Turkey will be canceled from September 21 until further notice. This news follows the cancellation of Mahan Airlines flights to Turkey and Oman. Mahan attributed the cancellations to decisions by Turkish authorities.

Greenpeace has identified five large oil slicks covering 240 square kilometers in the Strait of Hormuz and around Oman. About 70 oil tankers carrying oil are trapped in the Persian Gulf. There is a possibility of more accidents and oil spills.

A Saudi official stated that Saudi Arabia will not show flexibility in normalizing relations with Israel even if Israel helps in confronting the Houthis in Yemen. From Riyadh's perspective, normalization is only possible with the resolution of the Palestinian issue. This report was provided by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have transferred their shares in Chelsea Football Club to Clearlake Capital. Clearlake now has full control of the club and paid nearly one billion pounds for these shares. Todd Boehly has also resigned from his position as club chairman.

Mohammad Taghi Asanlou, Deputy Operations of the Armed Forces General Staff, called for an end to the US presence in West Asia. He described the US presence as an obstacle to peace and stability. He also emphasized that the country's security relies on indigenous defense capabilities and public support.

A citizen reported the extensive deployment of special unit vehicles and armed officers at Park Square in Mashhad on the evening of September 16. The presence aims to prevent protest gatherings. Forces have increased at intersections.

The Faculty Syndicate Council of Shiraz University announced the suspension of all educational, research, and executive activities from Saturday, September 18, until further notice. This decision was made due to repeated follow-ups on legal rulings and rights of faculty members and unresolved related issues. The council also expressed support for the announcement of the Iranian University Professors' Syndicate regarding the suspension of academic activities from the new semester.

Amnesty International stated in a report of over 1100 pages that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in suppressing the Mahsa uprising. Seventy percent of the victims were under 30 years old. Torture of detainees was widespread and systematic.

Diana Al Tahawi, senior advisor at Amnesty International, described the organization's report of over a thousand pages on the suppression of the Women, Life, Freedom movement. The report includes extensive evidence of killings, torture, sexual violence, enforced disappearances, and widespread arrests. Al Tahawi called these crimes systematic and organized and called for international mechanisms to hold responsible officials accountable.

Yisrael Katz stated that Israel will not allow the Iranian government or any other party to rearm Hamas. He said the Israeli operation is not over and that Israel has objectives against the Islamic Republic. Katz added that Israel will continue military and political actions to achieve these goals.

The head of Tehran's Safety Commission announced that 48 buildings remain in a critical condition. So far, 81 out of 129 very high-risk buildings have been removed from this status. Issues such as weak regulations, safety costs, and neglect by some institutions are obstacles to building safety.
A citizen told Iran International that his refrigerator has been empty for a week. He stated that he has had no income for some time and has no savings. This indicates his financial difficulties.

Some insurance services and medications have been cut, and medical costs without insurance are very high. Prices of essential goods like baby formula and diapers have increased significantly. The Tapico company affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards has started widespread layoffs of local workers in Khark, and surveillance cameras are being enhanced in major cities.

The trial of Mehran Mohaqqeqi, accused of a car attack on an Iranian gathering in Toronto, ended again without result and was postponed to next month. Repeated delays and the release of the accused on bail have sparked criticism. This issue has been criticized by Iranians and the Conservative Party of Canada.

Heavy rain has caused the cancellation of the women's cricket match between Bangladesh and China at the Asian Games. There are concerns about the weather affecting the opening ceremony. It is still unclear whether the opening ceremony will be delayed or if there will be other changes to the schedule.

Four years have passed since the start of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising, in which Iranian athletes participated. Several athletes, including Ali Mozaffari, Mohammad Ghaemifar, Ehsan Ghasemifar, and Ghazaleh Chalabi, were killed during these protests. Amir Nasrazadani remains imprisoned.

Following the release of a video showing violent treatment of a detained teenager in Tabriz by police officers, the East Azerbaijan police commander announced disciplinary action against the involved officers. The video shows the teenager being beaten and threatened with sexual assault. This incident occurred at a police station.

Security pressures on the families of the disappeared from the January protests continue. Reports indicate summons, SIM card blocking, and closure of their social media pages. This issue was discussed in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.

Amir Ali Sharei's brother joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and asked people to keep his memory alive. Amir Ali Sharei was killed on January 9, 2026, in Vali Asr Street, Tehran. The video was released with music.

A video showing violence by several police officers against a child in East Azerbaijan has been released. The incident occurred on June 4 after the child's arrest, and the officers have been suspended. Their case is under investigation for possible punishment.

Faleh al-Fayyadh, head of Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces, traveled to Turkey four months ago to explore transferring his personal assets. Turkey did not approve his request to transfer the assets. Additionally, financial pressures have been applied to his activities in Qatar, which opposed keeping his assets there.

Hatam Ahmadi stated that legal steps have been taken to recruit Alireza Jahanbakhsh as a soldier for Fajr Sepasi, and necessary approvals have been obtained. If the transfer is finalized, Jahanbakhsh will serve his military duty playing for Fajr Sepasi. This comes as several other players have also become subject to military service and need to resolve their conscription status.

A video has been released showing police officers physically assaulting and sexually harassing a teenager in Tabriz. The East Azerbaijan police commander stated the incident occurred on June 4, 2026, and the officers have been disciplined. The video has sparked widespread reactions on social media.

The police commander of Zabol announced the closure of a recreational complex in the city. The reason for the closure was stated as non-compliance with Islamic codes and lack of hijab. This action took place in Zabol.

China has privately asked Iran to help control the Houthi rebels in Yemen following a request from Saudi Arabia. This request came after the Houthis advanced along the Red Sea coasts and near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Iran responded that regional stability depends on the end of the war between the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic.

Iran and China's oil and trade exchanges pass through a multi-layer financial network. Revenue from Iran's oil sales is transferred to a Chinese entity and used for infrastructure projects and purchasing goods from China. About two to two and a half billion dollars have passed through this financial route in the past year.

Esmaeil Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, condemned any attacks on Islamic holy sites, especially Mecca, Medina, and Al-Aqsa Mosque. He also stated that Saudi Arabia's report on intercepting a drone near Mecca cannot be used to accuse the Houthis of the attack. These remarks were published on the X network.

Sediqeh Kamali, the wife of the late Sajad Dehghani, joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Sajad Dehghani was killed by two bullets in Bandar Abbas on the night of January 9. The video was published on social media.

Officials from the Kurdistan Region of Iraq met with the Islamic Republic in Tehran. This meeting coincided with ongoing attacks by the Islamic Republic on Kurdish areas along the Iran border. The Kurdistan Region aims to reassure Tehran that no ground operations will be launched from this area.

Etemad newspaper reported an increase in students' educational expenses for the new year. The initial costs for a student in a public school for a family with average income are estimated at least 15 million tomans. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mansoureh Hosseini-Yeganeh.

Majid Ibn al-Reza stated that US Patriot, THAAD systems, and Tomahawk missiles faced challenges against Iran's missile and drone technology in the recent war. He said the country's deterrence capability is managed by the Ministry of Defense and the production of new military systems will continue. He also emphasized increasing women's roles in defense industries and announced programs to recruit and empower female specialists.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated that he has completed a major part of his mission against the Islamic Republic. He said at a ceremony honoring Shabak employees that Israel will defeat the Islamic Republic. He also emphasized efforts to overthrow this regime.

Installment purchasing in Iran is no longer limited to homes, cars, or household appliances and has extended to groceries and daily family expenses. This trend coincides with the decline in people's purchasing power and the entry of more credit companies into daily life. The government is also seeking to expand the credit purchase policy.

Mohammad Baqer Zolghadr stated that the Islamic Republic forces will not open the Strait of Hormuz until Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu are removed from power. He said the Islamic Republic intends to avenge the killing of Ali Khamenei and thousands of others. He described the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz as the first stage of this revenge.

The UN Security Council is voting on extending the mandate of the expert panel monitoring sanctions on Iran. The draft resolution was presented by the United States. Russia and China oppose the move due to disagreements over the validity of the snapback mechanism.

China and Russia vetoed the US draft resolution to extend the mandate of the expert panel monitoring sanctions on the Islamic Republic at the UN Security Council meeting. The draft resolution received 11 votes in favor, two against, and two abstentions. It was not approved due to the negative votes of China and Russia.

Russia and China vetoed the draft resolution to extend the mandate of the expert panel of sanctions committee 1737 against Iran at the UN Security Council meeting. The resolution received 11 positive votes, 2 vetoes, and 2 abstentions. Russia and China believe that with the expiration of resolution 2231 in 2025, the sanctions mechanisms will lose their legal validity.

The Teachers' Union issued a statement commemorating the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's death and honoring her and the Women, Life, Freedom movement. The statement described her death as the beginning of a wave of protests and social demands. These protests have led to a profound change in Iranian society.

Axel Wilhelm Ditman, the German ambassador in Tehran, was summoned to the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The summons followed statements by German officials and Tehran's protest against what it called the embassy's interventionist actions. The Director General for Western Europe at the Iranian Foreign Ministry rejected the German Chancellor's remarks and condemned Germany's support for Israel.

The vote count for the Swedish parliamentary elections has ended, and opposition parties won a majority by a margin of three seats. The Swedish Prime Minister resigned after the results were announced. The process of forming a new government will begin.

Amir Ghalenoei announced the first national team roster after the World Cup. The list does not include Hossein Kanaani-Zadegan, Ali Alipour, and Roozbeh Cheshmi. The roster features players from the Persian Gulf Pro League.
The removal of mandatory hijab has reduced expenses on buying mantos and scarves. People feel more comfortable, confident, and free. Additionally, hair health and vitamin D absorption have improved.

Four years have passed since the death of Zhina Mahsa Amini in the custody of the morality police. This death led to the formation of the widespread Woman, Life, Freedom movement. Khaled Azizi, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran, has evaluated the changes this movement has brought to Iranian society.

Masoud Behnoud, a journalist and writer, announced in an interview that he intends to return to Iran. The head of the Basij Organization also spoke about the necessity of the return of those who are regretful. This comes amid the continued return of some figures and activists supporting the Islamic Republic to Iran.

The niece of Ramin Sahari Kismi, a protester killed in Tehran, joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. She stated that the names of the protesters will never be forgotten. This video was shared on social media.

Joseph Aoun welcomed the progress of preliminary Paris talks to support the Lebanese army and internal security forces. He appreciated the efforts of France, Jordan, and the participation of various countries. He also emphasized protecting sovereignty and the monopoly of weapons by the Lebanese government.

The European Union condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including an attempted drone attack on Mecca. It stated that these attacks undermine the prospects for a peaceful resolution in Yemen and threaten regional security. The EU called on the Houthis to cease all military actions and remain committed to peace.

Abdulmalik al-Houthi, leader of Yemen's Houthis, denied the claim that his forces targeted Mecca and called it a great slander. He accused Saudi Arabia of trying to encourage other countries to join the conflict by raising this issue. Al-Houthi called on Muslims to take a stance against this action by Saudi Arabia.

The CEO of the Charity Association for Cancer Patients in Kermanshah reported a sharp increase in treatment costs and insurance problems for patients. The cost of some medicines has reached 40 to 50 million tomans per month, and patients have resorted to selling essential household items to cover expenses. Social Security insured individuals must pay about 39 million tomans for PET scans.

Four years have passed since the start of the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising, in which athletes and football fans participated. Several athletes and football fans lost their lives during the protests. Among them were Sarina Esmaeilzadeh and Aryan Moridi.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported suspicious activity 75 nautical miles east of Aden. A tanker moving west reported being followed and attempted to be stopped by a small boat. The incident occurred on Thursday, September 17 at 17:29 Iran time and is under investigation.

Mohammad Rashidi, a member of the parliament's presiding board, said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the Islamic Republic's seven conditions in the Islamabad agreement are met. He said lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, and ending the war are among these conditions. Rashidi accused the US of violating the Islamabad agreement and continuing the naval blockade and sanctions, and said the US should not interfere in regional issues.

Manouchehr Motaki, Tehran representative, said diplomacy does not always mean negotiation and sometimes means not negotiating. He emphasized that the outcome of the war will determine the future order of the region and the next 90 days are very important. He also stated that the US does not intend to implement the agreement and only wants negotiations to continue so they can win the elections.

The death sentences of Mehran Babamir, Ehsan Amiri, Farid Khaledi, and Saeed Norouzi have been confirmed on charges of moharebeh. Previously, the death sentence of Ali Rahimi Rigi was also confirmed. The number of detainees from the December protests facing the risk of execution has reached at least five.

A viewer of Iran International reported a drawing by their child referring to the death of the former leader of the Islamic Republic. Children at school and in their communications talk about the coming of the Shah and the death of Mousa Ali. Even children from religious families opposing the regime are eagerly awaiting freedom and the return of the Shah.

Four years have passed since the killing of Mahsa Zeinab Amini in the custody of the morality police, which sparked a nationwide uprising and the "Women, Life, Freedom" movement. Athletes played a prominent role in this uprising, and four of them were sentenced to death. These individuals include Majidreza Rahnavard, Mohammadmahdi Karami, Kian Hosseini, and Saleh Mirhashmi.

The Italian defense minister announced that Italy is preparing to protect its commercial ships in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and will not wait for the EU naval mission's decision. The Italian navy and intelligence systems are ready to ensure the safe passage of ships. It was also warned that disruptions in shipping routes could increase costs and prices, and underwater infrastructures need protection.

Axios reported that Donald Trump, the US President, is on the verge of deciding whether to resume widespread attacks against the Islamic Republic. Trump stated that he has a big decision ahead and is scheduled to meet with leaders of Arab countries on Tuesday to hear their views on continuing the war. He also expressed satisfaction with the performance of the naval blockade and the prevention of Iranian oil exports.

The Institute for Science and International Security reported that the Islamic Republic began rebuilding the Taleqan 2 facilities in Parchin since June 1405. A cover has been installed to hide reconstruction activities, and heavy construction equipment is active. The institute described the purpose of the reconstruction as unclear and called the action concerning.

Due to sanctions, the American Law School Admission Council has canceled the registration of applicants with Iranian nationality or background. This action follows the intensification of US sanctions and restrictions against the Islamic Republic. The report is by Mahsa Mortazavi, a journalist from Iran International.
